<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
A packed caller that marks its trailing rows as padding gives the AITER grouped-varlen kernel a second `cu_seqlens` segment covering only padding. The kernel partitions work across segments, so the extra one costs part of every call. Attend the live prefix as a single segment and zero the tail, reusing the `trailing_padding_used_len` contract the FA and Sage backends already implement.

MiniMax-H3 packs one request into a single sequence and pads it to a multiple of 64, giving `cu_seqlens = [0, used, seq_len]`. The alignment tail is therefore a second varlen segment containing nothing but padding.

AITER's grouped-varlen kernel partitions work across segments, so that second segment costs part of every attention call. The cost tracks the segment count, not the padding rows: with the aiter kernel at 7 heads, head_dim 128, bf16, a zero-row tail and a one-row tail are within 0.1% of each other, while collapsing to a single segment is consistently faster.


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Added single-segment varlen handling to the AITER attention backend for packed callers whose trailing rows are padding.
- `AITerImpl` now opts into the existing `packed_trailing_padding` contract, reusing the `trailing_padding_used_len` helper already shared by the FlashAttention and Sage backends.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
### Before
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e8bd6f8-db17-413c-9dba-7d40b287c1b9


### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd0cd48b-b830-4060-8642-1de110b3883a


No change in output.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

### Microbenchmarks

Comparing `[0, N, N]` against `[0, N]` over the same N rows:

| rows | gfx942 | gfx950 |
|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 2.28 → 2.32 ms | 1.24 → 1.02 ms |
| 65536 | 33.47 → 29.23 ms | 16.75 → 15.28 ms |
| 104448 | 79.55 → 77.17 ms | 41.79 → 39.62 ms |


Comparing the full `[0, used, total]` call against the live prefix `[0, used]`
plus a zeroed tail, over the same `total` rows:

| rows (total) | gfx950 |
|---|---|
| 16384 | 1.23 → 1.03 ms (−16.1%) |
| 65536 | 17.00 → 15.52 ms (−8.7%) |
| 104448 | 41.44 → 39.00 ms (−5.9%) |

H3 produces 28K–109K packed rows across the supported 768p / 4–15 s range, so
this is paid on every denoising step of every request.

@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@

+    trailing_padding_used_len,
 )
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import AttentionBackendEnum
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms.aiter import (
@@ -250,6 +251,29 @@ def get_builder_cls() -> type["AttentionMetadataBuilder"]:
         raise NotImplementedError("AITer backend does not have a metadata builder.")
 
 
+def _live_prefix_len(
+    *,
+    total_tokens: int,
+    max_seqlen: int,
+    bounds: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> int | None:
+    """Live row count of a packed single sequence, with or without a tail."""
+    used = trailing_padding_used_len(
+        total_tokens=total_tokens, max_seqlen=max_seqlen, bounds=bounds
+    )
+    if used is not None:
+        return used
+    # The shared contract requires a non-empty tail because its callers pay a
+    # zeroed allocation to drop one. AITER hands the kernel's result back
+    # untouched when the tail is empty, so [0, N, N] is worth collapsing too.
+    if len(bounds) != 3:
+        return None
+    start, live, total = bounds
+    if start != 0 or live != total or total != total_tokens or live != max_seqlen:
+        return None
+    return live
+
+
 class AITerImpl(AttentionImpl):
     """
     Implementation of attention using AITemplate.
@@ -278,6 +302,11 @@ def __init__(
         self.causal = causal
         self.dropout_p = dropout_p
         self.softmax_scale = softmax_scale
+        # Packed callers whose trailing rows are padding; the grouped kernel
+        # is then given the live prefix as a single segment.
+        self.packed_trailing_padding = extra_impl_args.get(
+            "packed_trailing_padding", False
+        )

     def _forward_fp8(
@@ -402,10 +431,46 @@ def forward_varlen(
         max_seqlen: int,
         cu_seqlens_host: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
     ) -> torch.Tensor:
-        del cu_seqlens_host

+        used = (
+            _live_prefix_len(
+                total_tokens=query.shape[0],
+                max_seqlen=max_seqlen,
+                bounds=cu_seqlens_host,
+            )
+            if self.packed_trailing_padding and cu_seqlens_host is not None
+            else None
+        )
+
         cu_seqlens = cu_seqlens.to(device=query.device, dtype=torch.int32).contiguous()
+        if used is not None:
+            # A trailing segment is work the grouped kernel partitions over
+            # even when it holds nothing but padding, or nothing at all.
+            live_cu_seqlens = cu_seqlens[:2]
+            live_output = attention_func(
+                q=query[:used].contiguous(),
+                k=key[:used].contiguous(),
+                v=value[:used].contiguous(),
+                cu_seqlens_q=live_cu_seqlens,
+                cu_seqlens_k=live_cu_seqlens,
+                max_seqlen_q=used,
+                max_seqlen_k=used,
+                softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale,
+                causal=self.causal,
+                how_v3_bf16_cvt=AITER_BF16_CVT_MODE,
+            )
+            live_output = (
+                live_output[0] if isinstance(live_output, tuple) else live_output
+            )
+            if used == query.shape[0]:
+                return live_output
+            output = live_output.new_zeros(
+                query.shape[0], query.shape[1], value.shape[2]
+            )
+            output[:used] = live_output
+            return output
+

+
+    MiniMax H3 pads its single packed sequence up to a 64-row multiple, so
+    cu_seqlens carries a trailing segment of nothing but padding that the
+    kernel still schedules work over. Attending the live prefix alone is
+    invisible in the live rows, so only a dispatch-level assertion catches a
+    regression back to the two-segment call.
+    """
+
+    def _varlen_call(
+        self,
+        *,
+        packed_trailing_padding: bool = True,
+        cu_seqlens_host: tuple[int, ...] | None = (0, LIVE_ROWS, TOTAL_ROWS),
+        max_seqlen: int = LIVE_ROWS,
+        return_tuple: bool = False,
+    ) -> SimpleNamespace:
+        pytest.importorskip("aiter", reason="AITer is a ROCm-only dependency")
+        from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends import (
+            aiter as aiter_backend,
+        )
+
+        calls = []
+        kernel_outputs = []
+
+        def fake_flash_attn_varlen_func(**kwargs):
+            calls.append(kwargs)
+            # Derived from q so the assertions can tell which rows were fed in
+            # and where the kernel's output landed.
+            out = kwargs["q"] * 2 + 1
+            kernel_outputs.append(out)
+            return (out, None) if return_tuple else out
+
+        impl = _impl_cls()(
+            num_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+            head_size=HEAD_SIZE,
+            softmax_scale=HEAD_SIZE**-0.5,
+            num_kv_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+            packed_trailing_padding=packed_trailing_padding,
+        )
+        qkv = torch.randn(TOTAL_ROWS, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE)
+        cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(
+            (
+                cu_seqlens_host
+                if cu_seqlens_host is not None
+                else (0, LIVE_ROWS, TOTAL_ROWS)
+            ),
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+        )
+        with patch.object(
+            aiter_backend.aiter,
+            "flash_attn_varlen_func",
+            fake_flash_attn_varlen_func,
+        ):
+            out = impl.forward_varlen(
+                qkv,
+                qkv,
+                qkv,
+                cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+                max_seqlen=max_seqlen,
+                cu_seqlens_host=cu_seqlens_host,
+            )
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            calls=calls, kernel_outputs=kernel_outputs, qkv=qkv, out=out
+        )
+
+    def test_live_prefix_is_attended_as_a_single_segment(self):
+        run = self._varlen_call()
+
+        (call,) = run.calls
+        for operand in ("q", "k", "v"):
+            self.assertEqual(call[operand].shape[0], LIVE_ROWS)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(call[operand], run.qkv[:LIVE_ROWS])
+        for bounds in ("cu_seqlens_q", "cu_seqlens_k"):
+            self.assertEqual(call[bounds].tolist(), [0, LIVE_ROWS])
+        self.assertEqual(call["max_seqlen_q"], LIVE_ROWS)
+        self.assertEqual(call["max_seqlen_k"], LIVE_ROWS)
+
+    def test_padding_rows_are_zeroed_and_live_rows_keep_their_offsets(self):
+        run = self._varlen_call()
+
+        self.assertEqual(run.out.shape, (TOTAL_ROWS, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(run.out[:LIVE_ROWS], run.qkv[:LIVE_ROWS] * 2 + 1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            run.out[LIVE_ROWS:], torch.zeros_like(run.out[LIVE_ROWS:])
+        )
+
+    def test_tuple_return_is_unwrapped_on_the_live_prefix_path(self):
+        # aiter returns (out, lse) for some configurations; the padded path
+        # has its own unwrap, and a tuple reaching new_zeros() raises.
+        run = self._varlen_call(return_tuple=True)
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(run.out[:LIVE_ROWS], run.qkv[:LIVE_ROWS] * 2 + 1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            run.out[LIVE_ROWS:], torch.zeros_like(run.out[LIVE_ROWS:])
+        )
+
+    def test_empty_trailing_segment_is_collapsed_to_one(self):
+        # H3's token refiner always packs [0, N, N]: the rows are trimmed, so
+        # the trailing segment holds nothing and only costs the kernel a
+        # partition. There is no tail to drop, so the result comes back as is.
+        run = self._varlen_call(
+            cu_seqlens_host=(0, TOTAL_ROWS, TOTAL_ROWS), max_seqlen=TOTAL_ROWS
+        )
+
+        (call,) = run.calls
+        self.assertEqual(call["q"].shape[0], TOTAL_ROWS)
+        self.assertEqual(call["cu_seqlens_q"].tolist(), [0, TOTAL_ROWS])
+        self.assertEqual(call["max_seqlen_q"], TOTAL_ROWS)
+        # Returned straight through: allocating and copying here would cost
+        # more than the empty segment it saves.
+        self.assertIs(run.out, run.kernel_outputs[0])
+
+    def test_full_sequence_is_attended_when_the_caller_does_not_opt_in(self):
+        run = self._varlen_call(packed_trailing_padding=False, max_seqlen=TOTAL_ROWS)
+
+        (call,) = run.calls
+        self.assertEqual(call["q"].shape[0], TOTAL_ROWS)
+        self.assertEqual(call["cu_seqlens_q"].tolist(), [0, LIVE_ROWS, TOTAL_ROWS])
+        torch.testing.assert_close(run.out, run.qkv * 2 + 1)
+
+    def test_full_sequence_is_attended_without_host_bounds(self):
+        # The live length is a host value; without it there is nothing to slice
+        # at, and reading it off the device tensor would sync every call.
+        run = self._varlen_call(cu_seqlens_host=None)
+
+        (call,) = run.calls
+        self.assertEqual(call["q"].shape[0], TOTAL_ROWS)
+        self.assertEqual(call["cu_seqlens_q"].tolist(), [0, LIVE_ROWS, TOTAL_ROWS])
+        torch.testing.assert_close(run.out, run.qkv * 2 + 1)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
